name: Quicksand
label: Revelation
lede: Four guys out of the youth crew slowed hardcore down, tuned it low, cut a melted candle onto a Revelation seven-inch, and handed the next decade of heavy music a blueprint it's still using.

eras.title: Six weeks to Don Fury's
eras.text: Walter Schreifels had written the songs that defined Gorilla Biscuits and played bass in Youth of Today. With players from Bold, Beyond, Burn, Collapse and Absolution he built something slower, lower and louder, and Revelation put it out before the year was over.

years.p: Schreifels on vocals and guitar, [[Tom Capone|88c3e80c-41b6-48c9-985c-26ad5d026abd]] on lead guitar, [[Sergio Vega|a4256437-7cad-40b7-a135-9767863c90cf]] on bass, [[Alan Cage|65d4abbb-054b-4106-a826-0cb2b306341e]] on drums. [[Charlie Garriga|4f24f7e7-bc37-45d1-8f60-99bc992cd780]] of [[Outface|2fabef87-f53f-4792-b05b-6d54a8517d4c]] plays second guitar at the first shows, then drops out.

years.h: Quicksand 7" · cut at Don Fury's Demo Demo
years.p: Four songs, recorded in April about six weeks after the band formed, at Don Fury's Demo Demo studio in New York. The melted candle on the sleeve wasn't the first idea: [[Tim Singer|f59575a6-de2d-4eb3-9d6c-a076dcbcd603]] drew an alternate cover that went unused.
years.xp:
One description that stuck, passed along by writer Anthony Pappalardo: 7 Seconds' New Wind crossed with [[Jane's Addiction|e3434cc7-d348-491a-9dc8-325af3d9086d]]. Kids who came for Gorilla Biscuits heard it and started tuning down and slowing down in their own bands.

Revelation's catalog lists a big first run split between black and white vinyl, and the record has been repressed ever since.

years.h: A van, [[Shelter|d5157104-76b1-4b8b-90c2-9ff994f940db]], [[Inside Out|0049c4d7-6459-4b54-a865-fd19969f427f]], and a dead engine
years.p: The first tour: New York to Buffalo, Cleveland, the Unisound in Reading and City Gardens, with Ray Cappo's Shelter and Zack de la Rocha's Inside Out. The engine seized on day one; Revelation's Jordan Cooper paid to fix it, and Quicksand missed their first set.
About a year after the seven-inch, they're topping the bill at a Boston room that held around 2,000.

eras.title: The Revelation kids go major
eras.text: Polydor signed a band that had one seven-inch and a lot of word of mouth. Quicksand spent the next three years on tour with everyone from Fugazi to White Zombie, made two major-label records, and split after a show in Hollywood.

years.p: Tours follow supporting [[Helmet|582fee78-d934-4603-9f5c-1729e0ca36b7]], [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]], [[Rage Against the Machine|3798b104-01cb-484c-a3b0-56adc6399b80]], [[Anthrax|b616d6f0-ec1f-4c69-8a79-12a97ece7372]] and [[White Zombie|cfe572bf-840f-4bed-934a-f69f4b1e90d4]] across North America and Europe.

q: By the time we did Slip, that was our biggest influence.
Walter Schreifels, on My Bloody Valentine
years.p: The debut LP re-cuts Omission and Unfulfilled from the seven-inch, and Dine Alone leads it off as the single. A cassette picked up on an English tour had rewired them.
years.xp:
The list of what went into it runs from [[Rites of Spring|b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b]] and [[Embrace|9d1ad8e3-8740-429a-bdc5-52f96a9c4431]] to [[Public Enemy|bf2e15d0-4b77-469e-bfb4-f8414415baca]], [[Wire|7f2a8098-50e3-451c-8696-c5d9f64f4762]] and the [[Cocteau Twins|000fc734-b7e1-4a01-92d1-f544261b43f5]]. The [[My Bloody Valentine|8ca01f46-53ac-4af2-8516-55a909c0905e]] tape was the one Schreifels singled out.

Thirty years later the reissue booklet collected tributes from [[Scott Ian|40b0dfb0-d7e7-4a92-b0fa-12ed9af54993]], Thursday's [[Geoff Rickly|132f1d42-4567-4dca-b6e1-3765726f91dc]], Refused's [[Dennis Lyxzén|d7bb37a5-3d48-4a2f-a761-fe66d5cdb409]] and Rise Against's [[Tim McIlrath|157e6a4c-5233-42f8-83f5-e43b0c04641a]].

years.p: The touring runs into 1994, with a US tour alongside The Offspring and the Freezing Process single.
The second major-label album reaches No. 135 on the Billboard 200. Delusional hits No. 2 on the CMJ chart, and Revelation presses the vinyl edition.
Quicksand are on the inaugural run of the traveling punk festival.
After a show in Hollywood, the band splits. The reasons given were fights inside the band and the grind of never getting off the road.

eras.title: Osaka, Boulder, and the album that never came out
eras.text: Two years apart was enough to try again. They reconvened in Japan, recorded in Connecticut, toured with a rising Deftones, and then the old tensions came back and took a third album down with them.

years.p: The first show since the split is in Japan. A Hawaii date after it gets cancelled.
Six months of new songs go down at Carriage House Studios in Stamford, Connecticut, with producer Steven Haigler.
The first North American show in three years, and an invitation to stay out on the road with Deftones and [[Snapcase|90f7f8df-db45-4a6c-89fb-9e912f77eabd]].
The old tensions return and the band stops indefinitely. The unfinished record and Manic Compression demos end up trading hands online, never officially released.
years.xp:
The 1998 run had gone well enough that Deftones asked them to stay out longer, and there were new songs from the Carriage House sessions. It wasn't enough to hold the band together.

For the next dozen years, the only way to hear what Quicksand did next was a bootleg.

eras.title: The special guest in Pomona
eras.text: In the gap, Schreifels made Rival Schools, Capone played in Handsome and Instruction, Cage joined Seaweed, and Vega became the bassist in Deftones. Revelation's 25th birthday got the four of them back on a stage, and five years later there was finally a new album, and one fewer member.

years.p: Billed only as a special guest on the fourth night of Revelation's 25th anniversary shows at the Glass House, the original four play together for the first time in 13 years. Five songs, including a cover of [[The Smiths|40f5d9e4-2de7-4f2d-ad41-e31a9a9fea27]]' How Soon Is Now?
years.xp:
The reunion came out of Revelation's own anniversary, the label that had put out the seven-inch 22 years earlier. By then Vega had spent years as the bassist in [[Deftones|7527f6c2-d762-4b88-b5e2-9244f1e34c46]], the band that had taken Quicksand out on tour in 1998.

Two months later they were at the Bowery Ballroom, and by January they were back on a full North American tour.

years.p: The Bowery Ballroom, their first New York show in 15 years, then Music Hall of Williamsburg the next night and FYF Fest in Los Angeles a week later.

years.h: The first North American tour in 15 years
years.p: And in August, a set at Belgium's Pukkelpop.

years.h: Illuminant, the first new song in 22 years
years.p: A 30-second clip the day before, then the single and a date for the album.

years.h: Capone leaves the tour in Phoenix
years.p: He misses that night's Crescent Ballroom show and heads home. The band finishes as a trio, with Schreifels covering all the guitar, and Capone doesn't return.
The first Quicksand album since 1995 goes to No. 1 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart.

eras.title: Three people, still loud
eras.text: As a three-piece, Quicksand made records faster than they ever had in the nineties. Stephen Brodsky of Cave In filled out the stage for a while, and a new label brought a fifth album in the summer of 2026.

years.p: A 12" EP on Epitaph, the first release without Capone.
Brodsky guests on Colossus, then joins the live band as touring guitarist, making them a four-piece again on stage through 2023.
Boston's Iodine Recordings reissues it from the original 1993 masters with a 64-page hardcover book of photos and posters and a foreword from Schreifels.
Released through Equal Vision, a sign of where the band was headed.

years.h: Bring On the Psychics on Equal Vision
years.p: The fifth album, announced in April with the new label deal. Stereogum made it Album of the Week.
